CITY LAUNCHES BIKE-SHARING PROGRAM

Riverside City launched its first public bike-sharing program on Monday. Residents can now rent bicycles from 40 stations across the downtown area using a smartphone app. — [1] —

Rating: ★★★☆☆ — Reviewed by Carla M.

I stayed at the Seaview Inn for three nights last week. The location is excellent — just a two-minute walk to the beach — and the staff at the front desk were friendly and helpful. However, my room was much smaller than it looked in the photos on the hotel's website, and the air conditioner was very noisy at night.

When I mentioned the noise, the manager moved me to a different room on the second night and gave me a voucher for a free breakfast. I appreciated this, but I think the hotel should update its website photos. I would stay here again only if the price were lower.

qs.q: What did the reviewer like about the hotel?
qs.e: "The location is excellent — just a two-minute walk to the beach" = vị trí rất tốt, 2 phút đi bộ ra biển. Phòng thì nhỏ hơn ảnh, điều hoà ồn.
w: chê: điều hoà ồn ban đêm

qs.q: What problem did she report?
qs.e: "the air conditioner was very noisy at night"; cô ấy phản ánh với quản lý.
w: lễ tân được khen thân thiện

qs.q: What did the manager do?
qs.e: "the manager moved me to a different room on the second night" = quản lý đổi phòng cho cô (kèm phiếu ăn sáng). Không hoàn tiền, không nâng hạng, không nói sửa điều hoà.
w: không hoàn tiền, chỉ tặng phiếu ăn sáng
không nói phòng mới tốt hơn

o: Change the photos on its website
qs.e: "I think the hotel should update its website photos" = khách sạn nên cập nhật ảnh trên trang web (update = change).
w: cô muốn giá phòng thấp hơn, không nói giá ăn sáng

The parking garage at Pinewood Business Center will be closed on Saturday, April 6, and Sunday, April 7, so that the floors can be repaved and new lines painted. — [1] — Vehicles left in the garage after 8 P.M. on Friday, April 5, will be towed at the owner's expense. — [2] —

LOCAL FARMERS' MARKET MOVES INDOORS
by Henry Choi

Every Saturday morning for the past eight years, farmers have sold fresh produce in the parking lot of Westfield Station. Starting in November, however, the Westfield Farmers' Market will move into the former Hartley Furniture building on Grove Street. — [1] —

Market organizer Ellen Price said the move will allow the market to stay open all year. "In the past, we had to close from December to March because of the cold," she explained. — [2] — The new building has room for 60 sellers, twice as many as the current location, and includes a small kitchen where cooking classes will be held.

Some shoppers have expressed concern about parking, as the Grove Street location has only 40 spaces. — [3] — Ms. Price said that the market is discussing an arrangement with a nearby church to use its parking lot on Saturdays. — [4] —

SMALL KNITWEAR BRAND GOES GLOBAL

When Anita Rao launched Kestrel Knitwear from her apartment six years ago, she sold handmade sweaters only at local craft fairs. Today, the company ships to customers in more than 30 countries and employs 45 people. — [1] —

Ms. Rao credits much of this growth to her decision to focus on online sales early on. "Instead of opening expensive shops, we invested in a good Web site and professional photography," she said. — [2] — The company also responds personally to every customer review, a practice that Ms. Rao believes has built strong loyalty.

Not everything has gone smoothly. Last winter, an unexpected rise in demand left the company unable to fill orders for nearly six weeks. — [3] — Since then, Kestrel has partnered with two additional knitting workshops and introduced a waiting-list system so that customers are informed of delays in advance.

Looking ahead, Ms. Rao plans to open the company's first physical showroom next spring. — [4] — "Customers keep telling us they want to touch the wool before buying," she said.

From: Victor Lam, Account Manager, Greenfield Mills
Date: February 14
Subject: Price adjustment

Dear Purchasing Team,

I am writing to let you know that, due to a poor wheat harvest in several growing regions, Greenfield Mills will raise the price of all flour products by 8 percent, effective April 1.

Victor Lam

MEMORANDUM
To: All research staff
From: Dr. Helen Moss, Laboratory Director
Date: May 12
Re: Equipment booking

Over the past few months, several teams have reported that the electron microscope was unavailable when they needed it, even though the booking calendar showed it as free. In many cases, staff had used the equipment without recording their sessions.

To address this issue, the following rules will apply from June 1:
1. All sessions must be booked through the online calendar at least 24 hours in advance.
2. Bookings are limited to four hours per team per day.
3. Unused bookings must be canceled at least two hours before the start time. Teams that fail to cancel three times in one month will lose booking rights for two weeks.

I recognize that these rules may seem strict, but they are necessary to ensure fair access for everyone. Please direct any questions to my assistant, Leo Carter.

CITY APPROVES RIVERFRONT HOUSING PLAN
by Laura Méndez · March 4

The Dunmore City Council voted 6–3 on Tuesday to approve a plan to build 400 apartments on the site of the former Calder Shipyard. The developer, Northbank Properties, has agreed to make 25 percent of the units affordable for low-income families. Construction is set to begin in the fall and should take about three years.

Supporters say the project will help ease the city's housing shortage. Opponents, however, argue that the plan does not include enough parking and that traffic on Harbor Road, already crowded during rush hour, will get worse. Council member Jorge Ruiz, who voted against the plan, said he would ask Northbank to pay for road improvements.
Letter to the editor

To the Editor:

I read with interest Laura Méndez's article about the riverfront housing plan (March 4). As someone who has lived on Harbor Road for twenty years, I share the concerns about traffic. However, the article left out an important fact: the plan also includes a public park and a walking path along the river, which residents have requested for a long time.

I believe these features make the project worth supporting, and I hope the council will follow through on Mr. Ruiz's proposal.

Nora Klein
Dunmore

SEASIDE KITCHEN OPENS ON PIER 9
by Rafael Ortiz · August 2

Seaside Kitchen, a new seafood restaurant, opened on Pier 9 last week. Head chef and owner Hana Kobayashi was previously head chef at Lumière in Montreal. Her menu focuses on seasonal seafood from local fishing boats.

The restaurant is open Wednesday through Monday, from 5 P.M. to 11 P.M. Reservations are recommended on weekends. The outdoor terrace, which seats 30, offers views of the harbor and is available on a first-come, first-served basis.
Online review

★★★☆☆ Reviewed by Peter Novak · August 18

My wife and I visited Seaside Kitchen on Saturday evening for our anniversary. We had booked a table on the terrace two weeks earlier, but when we arrived, we were told the terrace was full, and we were seated inside near the kitchen door. The grilled fish was excellent, and the lemon cake was the best dessert I've had in years. Still, the mix-up with our table was disappointing.
Response

Response from the owner · August 19

Dear Mr. Novak,

Thank you for your kind words about our food, and I am sorry about the problem with your table. As mentioned when we opened, terrace seats cannot be reserved. It seems the staff member who took your booking did not explain this to you. We have since reviewed our booking process with all of our staff. I would like to invite you both back for a complimentary dessert on your next visit.

Hana Kobayashi

VANCOUVER — Skyway Air, a regional airline based in Vancouver, will begin flying to four new cities next spring. — [1] — The new routes will connect Vancouver with Boise, Spokane, Reno, and Sacramento, cities that currently have no direct flights to western Canada.

To: All Employees
From: Rachel Osei, Head of Security
Date: September 2
Subject: New visitor procedures

Beginning Monday, September 15, all visitors to our headquarters must be registered in advance through the online visitor system. Employees expecting a guest should enter the visitor's name, company, and expected arrival time at least one business day before the visit.

CENTRAL RAIL — LOST PROPERTY

If you have lost an item on one of our trains or at a station, please complete the online lost property form as soon as possible. Include a detailed description of the item, the date and time of your journey, and, if possible, your seat or carriage number.

NAIROBI — A local technology start-up has developed a mobile app that allows small farmers to sell their products directly to restaurants and shops. — [1] — The app, called FarmLink, was launched in January and already has more than 8,000 registered users.

Traditionally, many farmers in the region have sold their crops to middlemen, who then resell them to businesses at a much higher price. — [2] — With FarmLink, farmers can see current market prices and receive orders from buyers in nearby towns.

Downtown Cafés Adapt to New Work Habits

SEATTLE — Before 2020, the Daily Grind café on Fifth Avenue served about 600 customers every weekday morning, most of them office workers on their way to work. — [1] — Today, that number has fallen to around 350, as many companies now allow employees to work from home two or three days a week.

Owner Ben Hartley has responded by changing the way his business operates. The café now opens at 8 A.M. instead of 6:30 A.M. and stays open later in the evening, when it hosts live music and board-game nights. — [2] —

Other downtown businesses have made similar changes. Several restaurants have started offering lunch delivery to nearby office buildings, while a bakery on Pine Street now sells most of its bread to shops in residential neighborhoods. — [3] —

Economists say that such adjustments will be necessary for some time. "Office attendance is unlikely to return to earlier levels," said Dr. Nadia Rahman of Westlake University. — [4] — "Businesses that adapt will be the ones that succeed."

Kinsley Paper Company was founded in 1952 by brothers Arthur and Henry Kinsley, who began by selling paper products from a small shop in Manchester. — [1] — Within ten years, the company had opened its first factory and was supplying paper to schools and offices across northern England.

CITY TO RAISE DOWNTOWN PARKING FEES

BRIGHTON FALLS — The city council voted 6–3 on Monday to raise the cost of street parking downtown from $1.50 to $2.50 an hour, starting on May 1. The council said the money would be used to repair sidewalks and improve lighting in the downtown area.

Council member Diane Cho, who supported the increase, said that higher fees would encourage more people to take the bus. "Right now, too many drivers circle the block looking for a space," she said. "This change will make it easier to find parking for those who really need it."

The city will also extend paid parking hours. Drivers will now have to pay from 8 A.M. to 8 P.M., instead of until 6 P.M. Parking will remain free on Sundays.

Some business owners have expressed concern that the higher fees will keep shoppers away.
Letter to the editor

To the Editor:

I am writing in response to your April 12 article about the increase in downtown parking fees. I own a small gift shop on Lake Street, and I believe the council has made a mistake.

Most of my customers stay for less than an hour, but many of them also visit the cafés and restaurants nearby. Paying an extra dollar an hour may not seem like much, but combined with the new evening charges, it will make shopping downtown less attractive than going to the Westgate Mall, where parking is free.

I agree that our sidewalks need repairs. However, the council should have considered other options, such as a small increase in business taxes, which would be shared more fairly. I hope the council will reconsider before the new fees take effect next month.

Sincerely,
Marco Bellini

MARLOW FOODS TO MOVE HEADQUARTERS

CLEVELAND — Marlow Foods, the maker of Sunny Grain cereals, announced on Tuesday that it will move its headquarters from downtown Cleveland to a new office park in the suburb of Westlake by next September.

The company said the move will allow it to bring together employees who currently work in three separate buildings. The new site will also include a product testing kitchen and a larger research laboratory.

About 600 employees will be affected. The company has promised to provide a free shuttle bus from downtown for staff who do not drive. The move is expected to save the company about $2 million a year in rent.

qs.e: Mời thầu cần giá cả mùa, 3 khách hàng, giấy bảo hiểm (thông báo); hồ sơ GreenEdge có giá $14,500, 3 khách hàng, đính kèm giấy bảo hiểm.
w: ✓ đủ giá, 3 khách hàng, giấy bảo hiểm

qs.q: What is suggested about Ms. Kovac's e-mail?
o: It was sent earlier than the stated date.
It was sent on the same day as the proposal.
qs.e: Mời thầu hứa báo kết quả trước 15/3; bà gửi thư ngày 12/3 → sớm hơn hạn đã nêu.

qs.q: How much will Carver Medical Group most likely pay GreenEdge in total?
qs.e: Giá cả mùa $14,500 + hệ thống tưới tự động $2,200 (bà Kovac đồng ý lắp) = $16,700.
w: chỉ là giá hệ thống tưới

qs.q: By when does Ms. Kovac want the watering system to be installed?
qs.e: Phải lắp xong “before the season begins”, mà mùa bắt đầu từ tháng 4 (mời thầu: “from April through October”).

gram: Carver Medical Group is seeking a company to maintain the grounds of its main clinic
seek + tân ngữ + to V = tìm … để làm …; the grounds = khuôn viên.
The selected company will be notified by March 15.
Bị động tương lai; by + ngày = muộn nhất là.
provided that the installation can be completed before the season begins
provided that = với điều kiện là; mệnh đề thời gian dùng hiện tại (begins).
vocab: proposal|noun|hồ sơ đề xuất / dự thầu|/prəˈpoʊzəl/|a formal offer to do a job for a price|We received five proposals.|Chúng tôi nhận được năm hồ sơ dự thầu.
grounds|noun|khuôn viên|/ɡraʊndz/|the land around a building|The hotel grounds are beautiful.|Khuôn viên khách sạn rất đẹp.
trim|verb|tỉa, cắt gọn|/trɪm/|to cut a small amount to make something neat|He trimmed the bushes.|Anh ấy tỉa các bụi cây.
certificate|noun|giấy chứng nhận|/sɚˈtɪfɪkət/|an official document that proves something|Attach a copy of your insurance certificate.|Đính kèm bản sao giấy chứng nhận bảo hiểm.
reference|noun|người giới thiệu, người xác nhận|/ˈrefɚəns/|a person who can describe your work or character|Please list two references.|Vui lòng ghi tên hai người giới thiệu.
provided that|conjunction|với điều kiện là|/prəˈvaɪdɪd ðæt/|only if|You can go, provided that you finish your work.|Bạn được đi, với điều kiện làm xong việc.

groups.t: Thông báo + sơ đồ cửa hàng + email · Trung tâm thương mại sửa chữa
pass: Notice

CENTRAL GALLERIA — RENOVATION UPDATE

Phase 2 of our renovation begins on Monday, September 8, and will last about ten weeks. During this time, the east wing on the second floor will be closed. Stores in that area will move to temporary locations on the first floor until the work is complete.

The main entrance on Grand Avenue will remain open, but the north entrance will be closed from September 8 to September 21. We apologize for any inconvenience and thank you for shopping with us.
Store directory

STORE DIRECTORY — TEMPORARY LOCATIONS (from September 8)

Trend Shoes — moved from 2-East 14 to 1-West 3
Pages Bookstore — moved from 2-East 18 to 1-Center 9
Little Steps (children's clothing) — moved from 2-East 21 to 1-West 7
Café Lumi — no change (1-Center 8)
Bright Optical — no change (2-West 5)
E-mail

To: Customer Relations, Central Galleria
From: Sophie Martin
Date: September 15
Subject: Bookstore

Hello,

I came to the mall yesterday to pick up a book I had ordered at Pages Bookstore. I parked near the north entrance, as I usually do, but it was closed, so I had to walk all the way around the building. Then, when I went upstairs to the bookstore, the area was blocked off.

I eventually found the shop, but only after asking an employee at Café Lumi, which is right next to it. There were no signs on the second floor telling customers where the stores had moved. I suggest putting up clear signs as soon as possible.

Sophie Martin

qs.q: What is the purpose of the notice?
o: To inform shoppers about construction work
To announce the opening of new stores
To change the mall's opening hours
qs.e: Thông báo giai đoạn 2 sửa chữa: khu phía đông tầng 2 đóng, cửa hàng chuyển chỗ tạm, cửa bắc đóng.
w: cửa hàng cũ chuyển chỗ, không phải mở mới

qs.q: According to the directory, which store has NOT moved?
qs.e: Bright Optical ghi “no change (2-West 5)” — nằm ở khu phía TÂY tầng 2, không bị đóng.

qs.q: Why was Ms. Martin unable to use the north entrance?
o: It was closed at the time of her visit.
She did not know where it was.
qs.e: Cô đến ngày 14/9 (email gửi 15/9, “yesterday”), trong thời gian cửa bắc đóng từ 8/9 đến 21/9 (thông báo).
w: cô vẫn thường đỗ xe ở đó
không nhắc chỉ cho nhân viên

qs.q: Where did Ms. Martin finally find Pages Bookstore?
o: In the center area of the first floor
In the east wing of the second floor
In the west area of the first floor
In the west area of the second floor
qs.e: Hiệu sách chuyển sang 1-Center 9, ngay cạnh Café Lumi (1-Center 8) — đúng như cô kể.
w: 1-West là chỗ của Trend Shoes, Little Steps

qs.q: What does Ms. Martin recommend?
o: Putting up signs to guide customers
qs.e: “I suggest putting up clear signs as soon as possible” = treo biển chỉ dẫn rõ ràng.
w: cô không đề nghị mở cửa bắc
không đề nghị chuyển hiệu sách về
nhân viên quán đã giúp cô

gram: Stores in that area will move to temporary locations on the first floor until the work is complete.
until + hiện tại đơn cho mốc tương lai.
I came to the mall yesterday to pick up a book I had ordered at Pages Bookstore.
Quá khứ hoàn thành (had ordered) cho việc xảy ra trước một việc quá khứ khác.
There were no signs on the second floor telling customers where the stores had moved.
V-ing rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ (= that told); câu hỏi gián tiếp where + S + V.
vocab: phase|noun|giai đoạn|/feɪz/|one part of a process|The first phase of the project is complete.|Giai đoạn đầu của dự án đã xong.
wing|noun|khu, cánh (toà nhà)|/wɪŋ/|a part of a large building|The east wing is closed.|Khu phía đông đang đóng cửa.
directory|noun|bảng chỉ dẫn, danh bạ|/dəˈrektɚi/|a list of names, places, or numbers|Check the store directory by the entrance.|Hãy xem bảng chỉ dẫn cửa hàng cạnh lối vào.
block off|phrasal verb|chắn, phong toả|/blɑːk ɔːf/|to close an area so people cannot enter|Police blocked off the street.|Cảnh sát chắn con đường lại.
eventually|adverb|cuối cùng|/ɪˈventʃuəli/|after a long time or many problems|We eventually found the hotel.|Cuối cùng chúng tôi cũng tìm được khách sạn.
put up|phrasal verb|treo, dựng lên|/pʊt ʌp/|to place something where people can see it|They put up posters around town.|Họ dán áp phích khắp thị trấn.
